noLicense.summary: What if I add no license at all?
noLicense.body: No license is not the same as public domain. Without one, default copyright applies and nobody may copy, modify or redistribute your code — a public repository is visibility, not permission.

refine.library: It is a library other software links against

permissive.label: Anyone can use it, freely
permissive.detail: Use, change, sell, ship in closed products — just keep the copyright notice.

copyleft.label: Improvements must come back
copyleft.detail: Anyone who distributes a changed version has to publish the source too.

community.label: I am contributing to an existing project
community.detail: The license is already decided — match the project you are contributing to.

non-software.label: This is not software
non-software.detail: Docs, data, design or media need a Creative Commons license, not an OSI one.

unsure.label: I do not know yet
unsure.detail: Get the low-regret default plus the two options worth knowing about.

flag.same-license: Same license for the whole work

iban.notEncoded: Not encoded by this country's format
iban.coverage: {n} countries with a registered IBAN format

reason.bad_charset: Not an IBAN shape — an IBAN is two letters, two digits, then letters and digits only
reason.country_unsupported: No registered IBAN format for this country code
reason.wrong_length_for_country: Too long for this country's IBAN
reason.structure_mismatch: Right length, wrong shape for this country's format
reason.checksum_failed: Checksum failed — there is a typo somewhere in this IBAN

secretScan.cleanCaveat: Nothing here matches a known credential format or reads as a random secret. Pattern matching is not proof — review anything you are unsure about.
secretScan.found: {n, plural, one {# possible secret found} other {# possible secrets found}}
secretScan.foundCaveat: Redact these before you paste this anywhere. If a key is real, rotate it.
secretScan.suppressedNote: Known demo values (EXAMPLE keys, your-api-key-here, repeated characters) are ignored so sample files do not cry wolf.
secretScan.truncated: Input capped — only the first part was scanned
secretScan.scopeNote: Detection only: this tool never contacts a vendor to check whether a key is still live — that would mean sending your key to a third party.

eanUpcGtin.operationCalculate: Calculate (code is missing its check digit)

reason.empty: Nothing to check on this line.
reason.non-digit-characters: Contains characters that are neither digits nor separators.
reason.unsupported-length: No GS1 identifier has this length (8, 12, 13, 14 and 18 digits are supported).
reason.length-mismatch: Wrong length for the type you selected.
reason.check-digit-mismatch: The final digit does not match the one the standard requires.

warning.separators-stripped: Spaces, hyphens and dots were removed before checking.
warning.all-zero: All zeros — mathematically valid, but not a real identifier.
warning.payload-is-also-a-complete-code: This is also a complete code length. If it already has its check digit, switch to Validate.

eanUpcGtin.truncatedRows: Showing the first {shown} of {total} rows. Copy and download carry all of them.

vin.privacy: Checked in your browser. The VIN is never sent anywhere.
vin.idle: Paste a VIN — the verdict appears as you type, no button.
vin.scope: Structure and check digit only (49 CFR 565.15 / ISO 3779). This is not a vehicle-history lookup.

verdict.keepTyping: Keep typing — {remaining} more characters to go
verdict.tooLong: Too long — a VIN has exactly 17 characters, this has {n}
verdict.invalidCharacter: Not a VIN character: "{char}" at position {position}

hint.confusable: "{char}" is never used in a VIN. Did you mean {suggest}?

notice.notProvenance: A valid check digit confirms the VIN is correctly formed. It does not confirm the vehicle exists, is unmodified, or has a clean history — a cloned VIN passes this check too.
notice.pre1981: Vehicles built before 1981, and some imported (JDM/European) vehicles, do not use this check digit — a mismatch may not mean the VIN was mistyped.
notice.partial: Check-digit validation needs the full 17-character VIN. A partial VIN is a decode job, not a checksum job.

uscc.invalid: Not a valid unified social credit code
uscc.illegalAt: Position {position}: “{char}” is not in the code character set (I, O, S, V, Z are excluded)

legacy.mismatch: Legacy check character would be {expected} — advisory only; not every registrant class carries a GB 11714 organisation code

uscc.divisionScope: Positions 3–8 are matched against the GB/T 2260 province table and the nesting rules of the six-digit form; the full county table is not carried.

note.incomplete: A unified social credit code has exactly 18 characters
note.illegalCharacter: Contains a character outside the GB 32100-2015 set (I, O, S, V and Z are excluded)
note.checkDigitMismatch: The check digit does not match the first 17 characters
note.departmentUnknown: Position 1 is not a registration department the standard defines (1, 5, 9, Y)
note.categoryUnknown: Position 2 is not an organisation category defined for this registration department
note.divisionUnknownProvince: Positions 3–4 are not a GB/T 2260 province code
note.divisionMalformed: A county under no prefecture, which GB/T 2260 does not allow

yamlDiff.originalPlaceholder: Paste or drop the original YAML (or JSON)
yamlDiff.changedPlaceholder: Paste or drop the changed YAML (or JSON)
yamlDiff.idle: Fill both panes and the comparison runs as you type.
yamlDiff.privacy: Both documents are parsed and compared in this browser — nothing is uploaded, which is the point for manifests carrying hostnames and secret names.
yamlDiff.resolveAnchors: Resolve anchors and aliases to their values
yamlDiff.parseFailed: One side did not parse — nothing was compared
yamlDiff.equivalent: No differences — the two documents resolve to the same structure
yamlDiff.equivalentStructural: Same resolved structure · {n} formatting or anchor differences
yamlDiff.documentCountMismatch: Document count differs: {original} vs {changed} — documents were paired in order and the extras reported whole

rule.keyOrder: Mapping key order, quoting and indentation are ignored; sequence order is compared, because a list's order carries meaning.
rule.anchors: Aliases are resolved to their values, so an edit behind a shared anchor shows at every alias site; an anchor or alias that changed with the value intact is reported separately as structural.
rule.mergeKeys: Merge keys (<<) are expanded before comparing, and a node's own keys win over merged ones.
rule.types: Type is part of the value: 8080, "8080" and !!str 8080 are reported as type changes, not as a generic change.
rule.sequences: Sequences of mappings pair by name, id or key when that field is unique on both sides, so one inserted item does not cascade; a reorder is still reported.
rule.blockScalars: Block scalars compare by resolved string, so the trailing newline that |- strips is a real change; a restyle with the same value is structural.
rule.comments: Comments are not part of the YAML data model and are not compared.
rule.multiDoc: --- streams pair document by document; a count mismatch is reported instead of comparing only the first.
rule.duplicateKeys: A duplicate mapping key in the input uses the last occurrence and is reported as a warning.

note.raw-text-mode: Raw-text mode compares characters, not structure: key order, quoting and indentation all count.
note.parse-error: One side did not parse, so nothing was compared.
note.document-count-mismatch: The two sides hold a different number of --- documents; documents were paired in order and the extras reported whole.
note.merge-keys-expanded: Merge keys (<<) were expanded before comparing.
note.anchors-unresolved: Aliases were compared as *name references, not as their resolved values.
note.yaml11-ambiguous-scalars: Unquoted y/n/yes/no/on/off read as strings here (YAML 1.2 Core) and as booleans under YAML 1.1 — quote them if a boolean was meant.
note.sequence-matched-by-identity: Sequences of mappings were paired by an identity field instead of by position.
note.duplicate-keys: A mapping declares the same key twice; the last occurrence was used.
note.truncated: Only the first 2000 changes are listed.
